summary.value: The Bureau of Construction Codes Licensing Section issues the state licences for this trade and reviews every application for compliance with the governing statutes.
summary.source_title: Bureau of Construction Codes — Licensing Section, Michigan LARA
summary.evidence: seeking licensure for Boiler, Electrical, Elevator, Mechanical, Plumbing, Inspector/Plan Reviewer, Residential Builder

jurisdiction_model.local_layer_note: One local layer is established and it is named on the board's own page: 'If you live in the City of Detroit, they issue their own licenses and registrations locally.' That sentence appears on the ELECTRICAL page only. No equivalent statement was found for mechanical or plumbing, and no other Michigan municipality was named on any page read, so the rest of the local layer is not established. 'state_and_local' is recorded rather than 'state_only' because it fails in the safe direction — it tells the customer to check the city as well — not because a mechanical or plumbing local licence has been evidenced.

boards.name: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, Bureau of Construction Codes — Licensing Section
boards.scope: Mechanical, plumbing, electrical, boiler, elevator, code-official and residential-builder licences and registrations, statewide

who_must_hold.value: Anyone contracting to install, alter or service mechanical work, or to pull a mechanical permit, in Michigan.
who_must_hold.source_title: Mechanical Examination, Licensing/Registration & Application Information — Michigan LARA BCC
who_must_hold.evidence: Licensed Mechanical Contractors can perform installations, alterations, servicing, and secure permits.

scope_note.value: The licence is per WORK CLASSIFICATION, and there are fifteen: hydronic heating and cooling and process piping; HVAC equipment; ductwork; refrigeration; limited and unlimited heating service; limited and unlimited refrigeration and air conditioning service; fire suppression; specialty; solar heating and cooling; solid fuel and vented decorative gas appliances; LP distribution piping; fuel gas piping; and fuel gas piping and venting.
scope_note.source_title: Mechanical Examination, Licensing/Registration & Application Information — Michigan LARA BCC
scope_note.evidence: Must take and pass an examination for each work classification desired.
scope_note.note: This is the field that surprises an out-of-state HVAC company most: Michigan does not issue one mechanical licence, it issues a licence carrying the classifications you qualified for, three years' experience and a separate examination EACH.

required.source_title: Mechanical Examination, Licensing/Registration & Application Information — Michigan LARA BCC
required.evidence: Must take and pass an examination for each work classification desired.

name.note: The bureau names no separate examination title beyond the work classification.

provider.source_title: Mechanical Examination, Licensing/Registration & Application Information — Michigan LARA BCC
provider.evidence: examinations are now conducted by PSI
provider.note: Approved applicants are contacted by PSI and choose one of five Michigan testing centres, six days a week. Since 14 June 2017 the examination fee is paid to PSI and must NOT be sent to the State of Michigan.

fee.note: Paid directly to PSI when the examination is scheduled; the bureau publishes no amount and says in terms that examination fees should no longer be submitted to the State of Michigan.

exam.note: Examinations may include questions from the Skilled Trades Regulation Act (2016 PA 407) and the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act (1972 PA 230) as well as the mechanical code itself.

requirement.value: Three years' experience in EACH work classification applied for.
requirement.source_title: Mechanical Examination, Licensing/Registration & Application Information — Michigan LARA BCC
requirement.evidence: Must have a minimum of 3 years experience in each of the work classifications applied for below.
requirement.note: Not three years in mechanical work: three years in each classification separately. A company adding ductwork to an existing refrigeration licence needs three years of ductwork experience and another exam.

alternatives.note: The bureau publishes no substitute for the three years on the mechanical page (its electrical page does allow credit for a recognised training programme; that is a different trade and is not carried across here).

application_fee.source_title: Application for Mechanical Contractor Examination & Licensing (BCC-11) — Michigan LARA BCC
application_fee.note: Initial mechanical contractor licence/classification, from the bureau's own application form BCC-11 (rev. 1/25). Adding a classification is prorated by where you are in the three-year cycle: $300 in year one, $200 in year two, $100 in year three. Veterans are fee-exempt. Application fees are non-refundable.

cycle.evidence: You must renew every three (3) years by 8/31.
cycle.note: Read from the 'Mechanical Contractor' section of the bureau's renewal page. Three years, on 31 August, and the bureau says in terms that not all mechanical contractor licences expire in the same year. Expired more than three years means re-apply and re-test.

fee.evidence: It is $300.00 to renew your license.
fee.note: Read from the 'Mechanical Contractor' section of the bureau's renewal page. The bureau prints the same sentence for several licence types, so the reading depends on the section, not on the sentence.

expiry_rule.evidence: You must renew every three (3) years by 8/31.
expiry_rule.note: A fixed calendar date, but NOT a common one: the bureau says in terms that not all holders of this licence expire in the same year, so the month and day are fixed and the year comes from the licensee's own cycle. Renewal opens 90 days before expiry.

grace_period.note: No grace period is published for the mechanical contractor licence. The bureau publishes only consequences — a $100 late fee, possible loss of the ability to pull permits or sign for applicants' time, and re-application with re-testing once expired more than three years. Recorded as not established, NOT as 'no grace period'.

late_fee.evidence: you have to pay a $100.00 late fee
late_fee.note: Read from the 'Mechanical Contractor' section of the bureau's renewal page.

required.evidence: You are not required to take code update courses for your mechanical contractor license.
required.note: A positive finding, not a gap: the mechanical contractor licence carries no continuing-education obligation at all, while the master and journey licences in the same bureau do carry the event-driven code update. A single 'Michigan CE' rule in a customer's spreadsheet is wrong for one of them.

hours.evidence: You are not required to take code update courses for your mechanical contractor license.
hours.note: Zero because the bureau says the course is not required for this licence, not because nothing was found. The holder may still owe a code update on another licence they hold — the bureau's own page says so in terms.

period.note: Not applicable: no hours are required for this licence type.

subject_breakdown.note: Not applicable: no hours are required for this licence type.

approved_provider_rule.value: Not applicable to this licence. Where a code update IS owed on another licence the holder has, courses and providers run through CE Broker.
approved_provider_rule.source_title: Electrical Examination, Licensing/Registration & Application Information — Michigan LARA BCC
approved_provider_rule.evidence: you can contact CE Broker to find all approved courses and providers
approved_provider_rule.note: The provider rule is quoted from the bureau's electrical page, which is where CE Broker is named; it is recorded here as the bureau-wide arrangement, not as a rule of this licence, which owes no hours.

carryover.note: Not applicable: no hours are required for this licence type.

delivery_constraint.note: Not applicable: no hours are required for this licence type.

required.note: No bond requirement appears on any page read (Licensing Section, renewals, mechanical, and the BCC-11 application form). Recorded as NOT ESTABLISHED, not as 'no bond required'.

general_liability.note: No liability-insurance minimum appears on any page read (Licensing Section, renewals, mechanical, and the BCC-11 application form). Michigan differs from Ohio here, which publishes $500,000 on the face of its requirements page — but an absence is an absence, and it is recorded as not established rather than as 'none required'.

workers_compensation.note: No workers'-compensation requirement appears on the pages read.

financial_responsibility.note: No credit or net-worth test appears on the pages read.

reciprocity_statement.note: NOT established for this trade. The sentence 'Michigan does not hold reciprocity with any other state/country' is published on the bureau's ELECTRICAL page, under 'Out of State Applicants', and nowhere on the mechanical or plumbing pages. Generalising it to this trade would be exactly the cross-source attribution error that pass B exists to catch, so it is not generalised. The product must render 'not established', never 'none'.

qualifying_individual_rule.note: No qualifying-individual rule is published for the mechanical contractor licence. Michigan requires one for plumbing (a master plumber representative) and for electrical (an associated master electrician) and says so on those pages; the mechanical page says nothing equivalent, and the difference is not assumed away here.

entity_registration.note: No entity-registration requirement is published by the bureau; corporate registration is a Michigan LARA Corporations Division matter, not a BCC one.

per_location_rule.note: No per-location or per-branch rule is published for mechanical contractors.

change_notification_deadline.note: No deadline is published for notifying the bureau of a change of qualifying individual for a mechanical contractor licence; the bureau publishes a 'Change in Contractor Info' form but no time limit on the pages read.

typical_timeline.value: Up to 3–5 weeks for the Licensing Section to process an application, reviewed in order of receipt.
typical_timeline.source_title: Bureau of Construction Codes — Licensing Section, Michigan LARA
typical_timeline.evidence: our processing time may be up to 3-5 weeks and applications are reviewed in order of receipt
typical_timeline.note: This is the bureau's own published figure for reviewing the application, not an end-to-end time to a licence in hand: it excludes scheduling and sitting the PSI examination, and for plumbing the separate hands-on practical, whose 2026 dates run monthly and are capped at 50–100 candidates and repeatedly 'at capacity'. Application fees are non-refundable and duplicate applications slow the queue.

coverage_notes: Michigan's local layer is modelled only where the bureau names it. The City of Detroit is named, on the electrical page. Every other Michigan municipality and county is not covered.
No bond position and no liability-insurance minimum could be established from any bureau page or application form read; both are left empty rather than guessed or borrowed from a neighbouring state.

PSI examination fees are set and collected by PSI, not by the bureau, and are not in this record. Since 14 June 2017 the bureau says in terms that examination fees should no longer be sent to the State of Michigan.

Michigan's Skilled Trades Regulation Act (2016 PA 407) and the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Act (1972 PA 230) are named on the bureau's pages but were NOT fetched: legislature.mi.gov did not respond to either attempt on 2026-09-04. Every statutory citation in this record is quoted as the bureau reproduces it, never from the statute itself.

The fifteen mechanical work classifications are described in the scope note but are NOT modelled as separate trackable objects. A Michigan mechanical contractor holding six classifications has one licence, one date and one fee in this record — which is correct — but the record cannot tell the customer which classifications they hold.
Michigan reciprocity is not established for mechanical. The bureau publishes its no-reciprocity statement on the electrical page only.

pass_a.method: fetched each source with kb-scripts/lib_kb.fetch (serial, 1.5 s spacing, two attempts, no retry on 403/404), read the normalised text in full, and recorded each value with a verbatim evidence fragment checked against the normalised page before writing

pass_b.method: two checks. (1) kb-scripts/verify_pass_b.py re-fetches every source_url over the network, independently of the pass-A cache, and asserts the evidence fragment is still literally present. (2) a separate semantic re-read of every source, re-deriving each value from the page rather than from the record, recorded per value in kb-data/_verification/<record>.md. A disagreement in either check demotes the value.
